q:
If '→' denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words
[dry → arid → parched] is analogous to [diet → fast → ________ ].
Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
exp:
dry → arid → parched: paani ki kami ki intensity badh rahi hai.
diet (kam khana) → fast (bilkul na khana, kuch time ke liye) → next level = starve (bhookh se mar jaana / lambe time tak khana na milna).
feast ulta meaning hai, reject/deny intensity chain me fit nahi hote.
Answer: (A) starve

q: If two distinct non-zero real variables x and y are such that (x + y) is proportional to (x − y) then the value of x/y
opts: depends only on x and not on y
depends only on y and not on x
exp:
Proportional ka matlab: x + y = k(x − y), k constant.
x + y = kx − ky ⇒ y(1 + k) = x(k − 1)
⇒ x/y = (k + 1)/(k − 1)
k constant hai, isliye x/y bhi constant hai (x ya y pe depend nahi karta).
Answer: (D)

q:
Consider the following sample of numbers:
9, 18, 11, 14, 15, 17, 10, 69, 11, 13
The median of the sample is
exp:
Pehle sort karo: 9, 10, 11, 11, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 69
n = 10 (even), to median = 5th aur 6th term ka average.
5th = 13, 6th = 14 ⇒ median = (13 + 14)/2 = 13.5
Trap: 69 outlier hai, mean (18.7) nikal ke option D mat choose karna.
Answer: (A) 13.5

q: The number of coins of ₹1, ₹5, and ₹10 denominations that a person has are in the ratio 5:3:13. Of the total amount, the percentage of money in ₹5 coins is
exp:
Coins = 5k, 3k, 13k.
Amount: ₹1 → 5k, ₹5 → 15k, ₹10 → 130k.
Total = 150k.
₹5 coins ka share = 15k/150k = 10%.
Trap: coins ki ratio (3/21 = 14 2/7%) ko amount ki ratio mat samjho.
Answer: (C) 10%

q:
For positive non-zero real variables p and q, if
log(p² + q²) = log p + log q + 2 log 3,
then, the value of (p⁴ + q⁴)/(p²q²) is
exp:
RHS = log(pq·9) ⇒ p² + q² = 9pq.
Dono side square: p⁴ + q⁴ + 2p²q² = 81p²q².
⇒ p⁴ + q⁴ = 79p²q².
⇒ (p⁴ + q⁴)/(p²q²) = 79.
Trap: 81 pe ruk jaana — 2p²q² subtract karna mat bhoolo.
Answer: (A) 79

q:
In the given text, the blanks are numbered (i)−(iv). Select the best match for all the blanks.

Steve was advised to keep his head __(i)__ before heading __(ii)__ to bat; for, while he had a head __(iii)__ batting, he could only do so with a cool head __(iv)__ his shoulders.
exp:
(i) 'keep his head down' = focus rakhna, low profile rehna.
(ii) 'heading out to bat' = batting ke liye bahar jaana.
(iii) 'a head for (something)' = kisi cheez ki natural talent/aptitude — 'a head for batting'.
(iv) 'a cool head on his shoulders' = shaant dimaag.
So: down, out, for, on.
Answer: (C)

q:
A rectangular paper sheet of dimensions 54 cm × 4 cm is taken. The two longer edges of the sheet are joined together to create a cylindrical tube. A cube whose surface area is equal to the area of the sheet is also taken.
Then, the ratio of the volume of the cylindrical tube to the volume of the cube is
exp:
Longer edges (54 cm) ko jodne se height = 54 cm aur circumference = 4 cm.
2πr = 4 ⇒ r = 2/π.
V_cyl = πr²h = π·(4/π²)·54 = 216/π.
Sheet area = 54 × 4 = 216 = cube ka surface area = 6a² ⇒ a = 6, V_cube = 216.
Ratio = (216/π)/216 = 1/π.
Trap: circumference 54 le liya to galat answer aayega — longer edges jud rahe hain, to woh height ban jaati hai.
Answer: (A)

q:
The pie chart presents the percentage contribution of different macronutrients to a typical 2,000 kcal diet of a person.
Pie chart (Macronutrient energy contribution): Carbohydrates 35%, Proteins 20%, Unsaturated fat 20%, Saturated fat 20%, Trans fat 5%.

The typical energy density (kcal/g) of these macronutrients is given in the table.
Macronutrient | Energy density (kcal/g)
Carbohydrates | 4
Proteins | 4
Unsaturated fat | 9
Saturated fat | 9
Trans fat | 9

The total fat (all three types), in grams, this person consumes is
exp:
Total fat energy share = 20% + 20% + 5% = 45%.
Fat se energy = 0.45 × 2000 = 900 kcal.
Fat ki energy density = 9 kcal/g.
Fat grams = 900/9 = 100 g.
Answer: (C) 100

q: A rectangular paper of 20 cm × 8 cm is folded 3 times. Each fold is made along the line of symmetry, which is perpendicular to its long edge. The perimeter of the final folded sheet (in cm) is
exp:
Har fold ke baad jo edge LONG hai, usko half karna hai.
Fold 1: 20 × 8 → 10 × 8 (long edge 20 half).
Fold 2: 10 × 8 → 5 × 8 (long edge 10 half).
Fold 3: ab long edge 8 hai → 5 × 4.
Perimeter = 2(5 + 4) = 18 cm.
Trap: teeno baar 20 wali side ko half karke 2.5 × 8 (perimeter 21) mat lo.
Answer: (A) 18

q:
The least number of squares to be added in the figure to make AB a line of symmetry is
[Figure: a horizontal dashed line AB. Unit squares drawn touching the line: left cluster — one square above the line, and below the line a row of two squares with one more square under the right one of them; right cluster (separate, to the right) — below the line a row of two squares with one more square under the right one.]
exp:
Line of symmetry AB ke liye: line ke ek side ka har square, doosri side pe mirror position pe hona chahiye.
Figure me zyada squares AB ke neeche hain, isliye unka mirror image AB ke upar banana padega (upar wala existing square bhi mirror se match hona chahiye).
Official figure ke hisaab se jitne neeche wale squares ka mirror upar missing hai, woh count karo — official key yeh count 6 deta hai.
Trap: sirf ek cluster count karke 4 ya 5 pe ruk jaana; dono clusters ke saare missing mirror squares gino.
Note: printed figure bahut chhota hai; exact alignment ke hisaab se answer figure pe depend karta hai — key ke according 6.
Answer: (A) 6

q: Let f: ℝ → ℝ be a function such that f(x) = max{x, x³}, x ∈ ℝ, where ℝ is the set of all real numbers. The set of all points where f(x) is NOT differentiable is
exp:
x aur x³ intersect karte hain jab x³ = x ⇒ x = −1, 0, 1.
x < −1: x > x³ ⇒ f = x; −1 < x < 0: x³ > x ⇒ f = x³; 0 < x < 1: f = x; x > 1: f = x³.
Har switching point pe slopes check: x=−1: 1 vs 3x²=3 (alag); x=0: 0 vs 1 (alag); x=1: 1 vs 3 (alag).
Teeno points pe corner ban raha hai ⇒ non-differentiable.
Answer: (D) {−1, 0, 1}

q:
The product of all eigenvalues of the matrix
[[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]]
is
exp:
Product of eigenvalues = det(A).
Rows: R2 − R1 = (3,3,3), R3 − R2 = (3,3,3) ⇒ rows linearly dependent.
Isliye det = 0 (matrix singular).
Answer: (B) 0

q: Consider a system that uses 5 bits for representing signed integers in 2's complement format. In this system, two integers A and B are represented as A=01010 and B=11010. Which one of the following operations will result in either an arithmetic overflow or an arithmetic underflow?
exp:
5-bit 2's complement range: −16 se +15.
A = 01010 = +10, B = 11010 = −6.
A + B = 4 ✓, A − B = 16 ✗ (15 se zyada ⇒ overflow), B − A = −16 ✓ (range me hai), 2B = −12 ✓.
Trap: B − A = −16 exactly representable hai, underflow nahi.
Answer: (B) A − B

q: Consider a permutation sampled uniformly at random from the set of all permutations of {1, 2, 3, ⋯, n} for some n ≥ 4. Let X be the event that 1 occurs before 2 in the permutation, and Y the event that 3 occurs before 4. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
opts: The events X and Y are mutually exclusive
The events X and Y are independent
Either event X or Y must occur
Event X is more likely than event Y
exp:
Symmetry se P(X) = 1/2, P(Y) = 1/2.
{1,2} ka relative order aur {3,4} ka relative order independent hain (disjoint elements), so P(X ∩ Y) = 1/4 = P(X)·P(Y).
⇒ Independent.
Mutually exclusive nahi (dono saath ho sakte), 'must occur' nahi (2..1..4..3 me dono fail), aur equally likely hain.
Answer: (B)

q: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
opts: In the cycle stealing mode of DMA, one word of data is transferred between an I/O device and main memory in a stolen cycle
For bulk data transfer, the burst mode of DMA has a higher throughput than the cycle stealing mode
Programmed I/O mechanism has a better CPU utilization than the interrupt driven I/O mechanism
The CPU can start executing an interrupt service routine faster with vectored interrupts than with non-vectored interrupts
exp:
(A) True: cycle stealing me har stolen cycle me ek word transfer.
(B) True: burst mode me poora block ek saath, throughput zyada.
(C) FALSE: Programmed I/O me CPU busy-wait (polling) karta hai, CPU utilization kharab hota hai; interrupt-driven I/O better hai.
(D) True: vectored interrupt me ISR address directly milta hai, polling/identification nahi karni padti.
Answer: (C)

q:
A user starts browsing a webpage hosted at a remote server. The browser opens a single TCP connection to fetch the entire webpage from the server. The webpage consists of a top-level index page with multiple embedded image objects. Assume that all caches (e.g., DNS cache, browser cache) are all initially empty. The following packets leave the user's computer in some order.
(i) HTTP GET request for the index page
(ii) DNS request to resolve the web server's name to its IP address
(iii) HTTP GET request for an image object
(iv) TCP SYN to open a connection to the web server
Which one of the following is the CORRECT chronological order (earliest in time to latest) of the packets leaving the computer ?
exp:
Step 1: Server ka IP pata nahi (DNS cache empty) ⇒ pehle DNS request (ii).
Step 2: IP milne ke baad TCP connection ke liye SYN (iv).
Step 3: Connection ke baad index page ka HTTP GET (i).
Step 4: Index page parse karke embedded image ka GET (iii).
Order: (ii), (iv), (i), (iii).
Answer: (C)

q: Given an integer array of size N, we want to check if the array is sorted (in either ascending or descending order). An algorithm solves this problem by making a single pass through the array and comparing each element of the array only with its adjacent elements. The worst-case time complexity of this algorithm is
exp:
Single pass me adjacent comparisons ≤ N − 1 ⇒ worst case O(N).
Worst case (e.g. array sorted hai) me poora array scan karna padega, N − 1 comparisons ⇒ Ω(N).
To worst-case = Θ(N), yaani O(N) aur Ω(N) dono.
Answer: (A)

Consider the following C program:

Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?
opts: The program gets stuck in an infinite loop
exp:
a = 6: loop condition 6 < 10 true.
a = 6/12 + 1 = 0 + 1 = 1 (integer division), a += 0 ⇒ a = 1.
Agli baar: a = 1/12 + 1 = 1, phir 1 ... a hamesha 1 rahega.

q:
Consider the following C program:
(see code)
Assume that the input to the program from the command line is 1234 followed by a newline character. Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?
opts: The program will terminate with no output
The program will terminate with 4321 as output
The program will terminate with 1234 as output
exp:
Har call ek char padhta hai; agar '\n' nahi hai to pehle recursive call, phir return pe putchar.
Calls: '1' → '2' → '3' → '4' → '\n' (yahan recursion ruk jaata hai, aur '\n' print nahi hota).
Unwinding me print order: 4, 3, 2, 1.
Output: 4321 aur program terminate.
Answer: (C)

q:
Let S be the specification: "Instructors teach courses. Students register for courses. Courses are allocated classrooms. Instructors guide students." Which one of the following ER diagrams CORRECTLY represents S?
(Entity sets = rectangles, relationship sets = diamonds.)
(i) Instructor —<Teaches>— Course; Course — [Registration] (drawn as an entity rectangle); Classroom —<Allocation>— Course; Course —<Student> (drawn as a diamond); Instructor —<Guides>— <Student>.
(ii) Instructor —<Teaches>— Course; Classroom —<Allocation>— Course; Course —<Registration>— [Projects]; Instructor —<Guides>— [Projects].
(iii) Instructor —<Teaches>— Course; Course connected directly by a line to [Classroom], with <Allocation> attached only to Course; Course —<Registration>— Student; Instructor —<Guides>— Student.
(iv) Instructor —<Teaches>— Course; Classroom —<Allocation>— Course; Course —<Registration>— Student; Instructor —<Guides>— Student.
exp:
Entities: Instructor, Course, Student, Classroom. Relationships: Teaches (Instructor–Course), Registration (Student–Course), Allocation (Course–Classroom), Guides (Instructor–Student).
(i) me Registration entity aur Student relationship bana diya — galat.
(ii) me Student hi nahi hai, 'Projects' extra entity — galat.
(iii) me Allocation diamond Classroom se connected nahi, Classroom directly Course se line se juda — galat.
(iv) me saare 4 relationships sahi entities ke beech hain.
Answer: (D) (iv)

q: In a B+ tree, the requirement of at least half-full (50%) node occupancy is relaxed for which one of the following cases?
exp:
B+ tree me har node (root ke alawa) kam se kam half-full hona chahiye.
Root ko exempt kiya jaata hai: root me minimum 1 key (2 children) bhi chal jaata hai.
Leaf aur internal nodes dono pe ⌈n/2⌉ wala rule lagta hai.
Answer: (A) Only the root node

q: Which of the following statements about a relation R in first normal form (1NF) is/are TRUE ?
opts: R can have a multi-attribute key
R cannot have a foreign key
R cannot have a composite attribute
R cannot have more than one candidate key
exp:
1NF ki sirf ek condition: saare attributes atomic (no multivalued / composite attributes).
(A) True: composite key (multi-attribute key) allowed hai.
(B) False: foreign key ka 1NF se koi lena-dena nahi.
(C) True: composite attribute atomic nahi hota, 1NF me allowed nahi.
(D) False: multiple candidate keys ho sakti hain.
Answer: A, C

q:
Let L₁, L₂ be two regular languages and L₃ a language which is not regular.
Which of the following statements is/are always TRUE?
opts: L₁ = L₂ if and only if L₁ ∩ L̄₂ = ϕ
exp:
(A) L₁ ∩ L̄₂ = ϕ ka matlab sirf L₁ ⊆ L₂; equality nahi (e.g. L₁ = ϕ, L₂ = Σ*). False.
(B) L₁ = Σ* lo ⇒ L₁ ∪ L₃ = Σ* regular. 'Always' false.
(C) Agar L̄₃ regular hota to complement lene pe L₃ bhi regular hota. So L̄₃ non-regular — True.
(D) Regular languages complement aur union ke under closed ⇒ True.
Answer: C, D

q: Which of the following statements about threads is/are TRUE?
opts: Threads can only be implemented in kernel space
Each thread has its own file descriptor table for open files
All the threads belonging to a process share a common stack
Threads belonging to a process are by default not protected from each other
exp:
(A) False: user-level threads bhi hote hain.
(B) False: file descriptor table process-level resource hai, saare threads share karte hain.
(C) False: har thread ka apna stack (aur registers, PC) hota hai.
(D) True: same address space share karte hain, ek thread doosre ka data corrupt kar sakta hai — koi protection nahi.
Answer: D

q: Which of the following process state transitions is/are NOT possible?
exp:
Valid transitions: New→Ready, Ready→Running (dispatch), Running→Ready (preempt), Running→Waiting (I/O), Waiting→Ready (I/O done), Running→Terminated.
Waiting→Running: nahi — pehle Ready queue me jaana padta hai.
Ready→Waiting: nahi — I/O request sirf running process kar sakta hai.
Answer: B, C

q: Which of the following is/are Bottom-Up Parser(s)?
exp:
Bottom-up parsers input se start karke reductions karke start symbol tak jaate hain.
Shift-reduce aur LR (LR(0), SLR, LALR, CLR) bottom-up hain.
Predictive aur LL(1) top-down parsers hain.
Answer: A, D

q: Let A and B be two events in a probability space with P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.5, and P(A ∩ B) = 0.1. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
opts: The two events A and B are independent
P(A ∩ Bᶜ) = 0.2, where Bᶜ is the complement of the event B
P(Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ) = 0.4, where Aᶜ and Bᶜ are the complements of the events A and B, respectively

q:
Consider the circuit shown below where the gates may have propagation delays. Assume that all signal transitions occur instantaneously and that wires have no delays. Which of the following statements about the circuit is/are CORRECT?
Circuit: input X goes directly to one input of a 2-input AND gate; X also goes through a NOT gate whose output is the other input of the AND gate. The AND output is Y (i.e., Y = X · X̄).
opts: With no propagation delays, the output Y is always logic Zero
With no propagation delays, the output Y is always logic One
With propagation delays, the output Y can have a transient logic One after X transitions from logic Zero to logic One
With propagation delays, the output Y can have a transient logic Zero after X transitions from logic One to logic Zero
exp:
Ideal case: Y = X·X̄ = 0 hamesha ⇒ (A) True, (B) False.
X: 0→1 pe NOT gate delay ki wajah se X̄ kuch der tak purana 1 hi rehta hai; us time AND ke dono inputs 1 ⇒ Y pe transient 1 (static-0 hazard/glitch) ⇒ (C) True.
X: 1→0 pe direct input turant 0 ho jaata hai, Y already 0 tha aur 0 hi rehta hai ⇒ transient 0 ka sawaal hi nahi (D) False.
Answer: A, C

q: TCP client P successfully establishes a connection to TCP server Q. Let N_P denote the sequence number in the SYN sent from P to Q. Let N_Q denote the acknowledgement number in the SYN ACK from Q to P. Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?
opts: The sequence number N_P is chosen randomly by P
The sequence number N_P is always 0 for a new connection
The acknowledgement number N_Q is equal to N_P
The acknowledgement number N_Q is equal to N_P + 1
exp:
Initial sequence number (ISN) random choose hota hai (security + old segments se confusion avoid) ⇒ (A) True, (B) False.
SYN ek sequence number consume karta hai, isliye SYN-ACK me ack number = N_P + 1 ⇒ (D) True, (C) False.
Answer: A, D

q: Consider a 5-stage pipelined processor with Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction Decode (ID), Execute (EX), Memory Access (MEM), and Register Writeback (WB) stages. Which of the following statements about forwarding is/are CORRECT?
opts: In a pipelined execution, forwarding means the result from a source stage of an earlier instruction is passed on to the destination stage of a later instruction
In forwarding, data from the output of the MEM stage can be passed on to the input of the EX stage of the next instruction
Forwarding cannot prevent all pipeline stalls
Forwarding does not require any extra hardware to retrieve the data from the pipeline stages
exp:
(A) True: forwarding/bypassing ki definition yahi hai.
(B) True: MEM stage output (e.g. load ka data) EX input tak forward ho sakta hai.
(C) True: load-use hazard me forwarding ke baad bhi 1 stall lagta hai.
(D) False: forwarding ke liye extra MUX aur forwarding paths/detection unit chahiye.
Answer: A, B, C

q: Which of the following fields is/are modified in the IP header of a packet going out of a network address translation (NAT) device from an internal network to an external network?
exp:
Outgoing packet me NAT private source IP ko public IP se replace karta hai ⇒ Source IP change.
Header change hua to IP header checksum recompute karna padta hai ⇒ Checksum change.
Destination IP same rehta hai; Total length bhi same (header size change nahi hota).
Answer: A, C

q: Let A and B be non-empty finite sets such that there exist one-to-one and onto functions (i) from A to B and (ii) from A × A to A ∪ B. The number of possible values of |A| is __________
exp:
Bijection A→B ⇒ |A| = |B| = n.
Bijection A×A → A∪B ⇒ n² = |A ∪ B|.
Par n ≤ |A ∪ B| ≤ 2n ⇒ n ≤ n² ≤ 2n ⇒ n ≤ 2.
n = 1: |A∪B| = 1, A = B lo — possible.
n = 2: |A∪B| = 4, A, B disjoint lo — possible.
Possible values {1, 2} ⇒ 2.
Answer: 2

q:
Consider the operator precedence and associativity rules for the integer arithmetic operators given in the table below.
Operator | Precedence | Associativity
+ | Highest | Left
− | High | Right
∗ | Medium | Right
/ | Low | Right

The value of the expression 3 + 1 + 5 ∗ 2 / 7 + 2 − 4 − 7 − 6 / 2 as per the above rules is __________
exp:
/ sabse low precedence aur right-assoc ⇒ expression = (3+1+5∗2) / ((7+2−4−7−6) / 2).
Left part: + pehle: 3+1+5 = 9, phir ∗: 9∗2 = 18.
Middle: + pehle: 7+2 = 9 ⇒ 9 − 4 − 7 − 6, '−' right-assoc: 9 − (4 − (7 − 6)) = 9 − (4 − 1) = 6.
Right: 6 / 2 = 3.
Final: 18 / 3 = 6.
Trap: normal C rules lagaoge to galat answer aayega.
Answer: 6

q: The number of spanning trees in a complete graph of 4 vertices labelled A, B, C, and D is _________
exp:
Cayley's formula: labelled complete graph Kₙ ke spanning trees = n^(n−2).
n = 4 ⇒ 4² = 16.
Answer: 16

q:
Consider the following two relations, R(A,B) and S(A,C):
R:
A | B
10 | 20
20 | 30
30 | 40
30 | 50
50 | 95

S:
A | C
10 | 90
30 | 45
40 | 80

The total number of tuples obtained by evaluating the following expression
σ_{B<C}(R ⋈_{R.A=S.A} S)
is _________
exp:
Join on R.A = S.A:
A=10: (10,20,90)
A=30: (30,40,45), (30,50,45)
A=20, 50 ka S me match nahi; S ka 40 R me nahi.
Ab B < C filter: 20<90 ✓, 40<45 ✓, 50<45 ✗.
Tuples = 2.
Answer: 2

q:
Consider a network path P—Q—R between nodes P and R via router Q. Node P sends a file of size 10⁶ bytes to R via this path by splitting the file into chunks of 10³ bytes each. Node P sends these chunks one after the other without any wait time between the successive chunk transmissions. Assume that the size of extra headers added to these chunks is negligible, and that the chunk size is less than the MTU.
Each of the links P—Q and Q—R has a bandwidth of 10⁶ bits/sec, and negligible propagation latency. Router Q immediately transmits every packet it receives from P to R, with negligible processing and queueing delays. Router Q can simultaneously receive on link P—Q and transmit on link Q—R.
Assume P starts transmitting the chunks at time t = 0.
Which one of the following options gives the time (in seconds, rounded off to 3 decimal places) at which R receives all the chunks of the file?
exp:
Chunks = 10⁶/10³ = 1000, har chunk = 8000 bits.
Ek chunk ka transmission time = 8000/10⁶ = 8 ms.
Pipelining: P ka last chunk t = 1000 × 8 ms = 8 s pe Q tak pahunchta hai.
Q phir use 8 ms me R ko bhejta hai ⇒ 8 + 0.008 = 8.008 s.
Formula: (N + hops − 1) × T = (1000 + 1) × 8 ms.
Trap: 16 s (poori file do baar) — store-and-forward per packet hota hai, poori file ke liye nahi.
Answer: (B) 8.008

q:
Consider the following syntax-directed definition (SDD).
(see code)
Given "MMLK" as the input, which one of the following options is the CORRECT value computed by the SDD (in the attribute S.val)?
exp:
Input MMLK: D → M M (ε), H → L (ε), T → ε, U → K.
D: innermost D→ε = −5; phir 5 + (−5) = 0; phir 5 + 0 = 5 ⇒ D.val = 5.
H: H→ε = −10; H = 50 + (−10) = 40.
T = −5 (koi C nahi).
U = 5.
S.val = 5 + 40 + (−5) + 5 = 45.
Answer: (A) 45

code:

T → aS | bT | (2)
R → (3) | ϵ

exp:

q:
Consider the following pseudo-code.
(see code)
Which one of the following options CORRECTLY specifies the number of basic blocks and the number of instructions in the largest basic block, respectively ?
code:
L1:  t1 = −1
L2:  t2 = 0
L3:  t3 = 0
L4:  t4 = 4 ∗ t3
L5:  t5 = 4 ∗ t2
L6:  t6 = t5 ∗ M
L7:  t7 = t4 + t6
L8:  t8 = a[t7]
L9:  if t8 <= max goto L11
L10: t1 = t8
L11: t3 = t3 + 1
L12: if t3 < M goto L4
L13: t2 = t2 + 1
L14: if t2 < N goto L3
L15: max = t1
exp:
Leaders: first instr L1; jump targets L3, L4, L11; jump ke turant baad wale L10, L13, L15.
Leaders = {L1, L3, L4, L10, L11, L13, L15} ⇒ 7 basic blocks.
Blocks: B1 = L1–L2 (2), B2 = L3 (1), B3 = L4–L9 (6), B4 = L10 (1), B5 = L11–L12 (2), B6 = L13–L14 (2), B7 = L15 (1).
Largest = L4–L9 = 6 instructions.
Trap: L3 ko leader bhoolna (L14 ka target hai) ⇒ 6 blocks aur 7 instructions galat aata hai.
Answer: (D) 7 and 6

q:
Consider the following two threads T1 and T2 that update two shared variables a and b. Assume that initially a = b = 1. Though context switching between threads can happen at any time, each statement of T1 or T2 is executed atomically without interruption.
(see code)
Which one of the following options lists all the possible combinations of values of a and b after both T1 and T2 finish execution?
exp:
T1: a=a+1; b=b+1. T2: b=2b; a=2a. Order within thread fixed, total 6 interleavings.
T1 poora phir T2: a=2,b=2 → b=4,a=4 ⇒ (4,4).
T2 poora phir T1: b=2,a=2 → a=3,b=3 ⇒ (3,3).
Mixed (a+1 pehle a*2 se, aur b*2 pehle b+1 se), e.g. a=a+1, b=2b, b=b+1, a=2a: a=2,b=2,b=3,a=4 ⇒ (4,3). Baaki mixed orders bhi (4,3) dete hain.
(3,4) impossible: a=3 ke liye a*2 pehle hona chahiye jo T2 ka last statement hai, tab b*2 already ho chuka ⇒ b = 3.
Answer: (A)

q: An array [82, 101, 90, 11, 111, 75, 33, 131, 44, 93] is heapified. Which one of the following options represents the first three elements in the heapified array?
exp:
Max-heap build (bottom-up), n = 10, i = 5 se 1 tak heapify.
i=5 (111, child 93): OK. i=4 (11, children 131,44): swap ⇒ 131 at 4.
i=3 (90, children 75,33): OK. i=2 (101, children 131,111): swap with 131 ⇒ pos2=131, pos4=101 (children 11,44 OK).
i=1 (82, children 131,90): swap ⇒ pos1=131, 82 at pos2; children 101,111 ⇒ swap with 111; 82 at pos5, child 93 ⇒ swap.
Final: [131, 111, 90, 101, 93, 75, 33, 11, 44, 82].
First three: 131, 111, 90. (Min-heap options A/B se match nahi karta: min-heap ka root 11 hota.)
Answer: (D)

q:
Consider the following recurrence relation:
T(n) = √n·T(√n) + n for n ≥ 1,
T(n) = 1 for n = 1.
Which one of the following options is CORRECT?
exp:
Dono side n se divide karo: T(n)/n = T(√n)/√n + 1.
S(n) = T(n)/n ⇒ S(n) = S(√n) + 1.
√ baar-baar lene se n → 2 tak log log n steps lagte hain ⇒ S(n) = Θ(log log n).
T(n) = n·S(n) = Θ(n log log n).
Answer: (A)

q: Consider a binary min-heap containing 105 distinct elements. Let k be the index (in the underlying array) of the maximum element stored in the heap. The number of possible values of k is
exp:
Min-heap me maximum element kisi internal node pe nahi ho sakta (uska child usse bada hona chahiye) ⇒ max hamesha leaf pe.
Leaves ki indices: ⌊n/2⌋ + 1 se n tak.
n = 105 ⇒ internal = ⌊105/2⌋ = 52, leaves = 105 − 52 = 53.
Har leaf pe max aa sakta hai ⇒ 53 possible values.
Answer: (A) 53

q: The symbol → indicates functional dependency in the context of a relational database. Which of the following options is/are TRUE?
opts: ((X, Y) → Z and W → Y) implies (X, W) → Z
(X → Y and Y → Z) implies X → Z
exp:
(A) False: LHS se attribute hata nahi sakte (XY → ZW se X → ZW nahi nikalta).
(B) True: decomposition rule — RHS split kar sakte hain.
(C) True: pseudo-transitivity — W → Y ⇒ XW → XY (augmentation), XY → Z ⇒ XW → Z.
(D) True: transitivity.
Answer: B, C, D

q: Let G be a directed graph and T a depth first search (DFS) spanning tree in G that is rooted at a vertex v. Suppose T is also a breadth first search (BFS) tree in G, rooted at v. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE for every such graph G and tree T ?
opts: There are no back-edges in G with respect to the tree T
There are no cross-edges in G with respect to the tree T
There are no forward-edges in G with respect to the tree T
The only edges in G are the edges in T
exp:
Forward edge u→w (w descendant, depth ≥ depth(u)+2) hota to BFS me w ko u se depth(u)+1 pe discover karna padta — contradiction. Isliye no forward edges (C) True.
Back edge possible: G = {v→u, u→v}; tree v→u DFS aur BFS dono ka hai, u→v back edge ⇒ (A) False.
Cross edge possible: G = {v→a, v→b, b→a}; DFS a pehle visit kare to tree {v→a, v→b} = BFS tree, b→a cross edge ⇒ (B) False.
(D) False: upar ke examples me extra edges hain.
Answer: C

Conflicts dhundo: z sirf T1 use karta hai ⇒ T1 ka kisi se conflict nahi.
x sirf T2 ⇒ koi conflict nahi.
y: r₃(y), w₃(y) pehle, phir r₂(y), w₂(y) ⇒ w₃(y)–r₂(y), r₃(y)–w₂(y), w₃(y)–w₂(y) ⇒ edge T3 → T2.
Precedence graph me sirf T3 → T2; T1 kahin bhi aa sakta hai.
Valid serial orders: T1T3T2, T3T1T2, T3T2T1.
T1T2T3 me T2 T3 se pehle — galat.
Answer: B, C, D

q:
Consider a Boolean expression given by F(X, Y, Z) = ∑(3,5,6,7).
Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?
opts: F(X, Y, Z) = XY + YZ + XZ
F(X, Y, Z) is independent of input Y
F(X, Y, Z) is independent of input X
exp:
Minterms 3 (011), 5 (101), 6 (110), 7 (111) — jahan kam se kam do inputs 1 hain ⇒ majority function.
K-map: XY + YZ + XZ ⇒ (B) True.
Maxterms = baaki = 0,1,2,4 ⇒ F = Π(0,1,2,4) ⇒ (A) True.
Majority function teeno inputs pe depend karta hai (e.g. X=1,Z=0: Y badalne se F badalta hai) ⇒ C, D False.
Answer: A, B

q:
Consider the following C function definition.
(see code)
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE about the above function?
opts: If the inputs are x=20, y=10, then the return value is greater than 2²⁰
If the inputs are x=20, y=20, then the return value is greater than 2²⁰
If the inputs are x=20, y=10, then the return value is less than 2¹⁰
If the inputs are x=10, y=20, then the return value is greater than 2²⁰
exp:
Har iteration: x = 2x + y, y baar chalta hai.
Closed form: x_final = 2^y·x + y(2^y − 1).
(x=20,y=10): 1024·20 + 10·1023 = 30710 ⇒ 2¹⁰ se bada, 2²⁰ (1048576) se chhota ⇒ A, C False.
(x=20,y=20): 2²⁰·20 + 20(2²⁰−1) ≫ 2²⁰ ⇒ B True.
(x=10,y=20): 2²⁰·10 + 20(2²⁰−1) ≫ 2²⁰ ⇒ D True (≈ 3.1×10⁷, int me fit).
Answer: B, D

q: Let A be any n × m matrix, where m > n. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE about the system of linear equations Ax = 0 ?
opts: There exist at least m − n linearly independent solutions to this system
There exist m − n linearly independent vectors such that every solution is a linear combination of these vectors
There exists a non-zero solution in which at least m − n variables are 0
There exists a solution in which at least n variables are non-zero
exp:
rank(A) ≤ n ⇒ nullity = m − rank ≥ m − n ⇒ (A) True.
(B) False: agar rank < n, to nullity > m − n; sirf m − n vectors poora null space span nahi karenge (e.g. A = zero matrix).
(C) False: A = [1 1] (n=1, m=2): solutions (t, −t); koi non-zero solution me 1 zero nahi.
(D) False: A = [[1,0,0],[0,1,0]] (n=2, m=3): solutions (0,0,t) — sirf 1 non-zero variable.
Answer: A

q:
Consider the 5-state DFA M accepting the language L(M) ⊂ (0 + 1)* shown below. For any string w ∈ (0 + 1)* let n₀(w) be the number of 0's in w and n₁(w) be the number of 1's in w.
DFA M (start state 1, only final state 1):
State | on 0 | on 1
1 | 2 | 4
2 | 3 | 1
3 | 1 | 2
4 | 1 | 5
5 | 4 | 1
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
opts: States 2 and 4 are distinguishable in M
States 3 and 4 are distinguishable in M
States 2 and 5 are distinguishable in M
Any string w with n₀(w) = n₁(w) is in L(M)
exp:
DFA (n₀ − n₁) mod 3 track karta hai: state 1 = 0, 2 = +1, 3 = +2, 4 = −1, 5 = −2. L(M) = {w : n₀(w) − n₁(w) ≡ 0 mod 3}.
+1 ≡ −2 aur +2 ≡ −1 (mod 3) ⇒ states 2 ≡ 5 aur 3 ≡ 4 (equivalent).
Check: 2 vs 5 — on 1 dono → 1; on 0 → 3 aur 4. 3 vs 4 — on 0 dono → 1; on 1 → 2 aur 5. Consistent ⇒ equivalent.
(A) 2 vs 4: string '1' — 2→1 accept, 4→5 reject ⇒ distinguishable (True).
(B), (C) indistinguishable pairs ko distinguishable bol rahe ⇒ FALSE.
(D) n₀ = n₁ ⇒ difference 0 ⇒ accept ⇒ True.
FALSE statements: B, C

q: The chromatic number of a graph is the minimum number of colours used in a proper colouring of the graph. Let G be any graph with n vertices and chromatic number k. Which of the following statements is/are always TRUE?
opts: G contains a complete subgraph with k vertices
G contains an independent set of size at least n/k
G contains at least k(k − 1)/2 edges
G contains a vertex of degree at least k
exp:
(A) False: C₅ ka χ = 3 par triangle (K₃) nahi hai.
(B) True: k colour classes me n vertices baante hain ⇒ koi class ≥ n/k; har colour class independent set hai.
(C) True: optimal colouring me har do colour classes ke beech kam se kam ek edge honi chahiye (warna merge kar dete) ⇒ ≥ C(k,2) = k(k−1)/2 edges.
(D) False: Kₖ me χ = k par max degree k − 1.
Answer: B, C

q: Consider the operators ◊ and □ defined by a ◊ b = a + 2b, a □ b = ab, for positive integers. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
opts: Operator ◊ over the operator □ obeys the distributive law
Operator □ over the operator ◊ obeys the distributive law
exp:
(A) (a◊b)◊c = a + 2b + 2c, a◊(b◊c) = a + 2b + 4c ⇒ not associative.
(B) □ = normal multiplication ⇒ associative ✓.
(C) a◊(b□c) = a + 2bc, (a◊b)□(a◊c) = (a+2b)(a+2c) ⇒ equal nahi.
(D) a□(b◊c) = a(b + 2c) = ab + 2ac = (a□b)◊(a□c) ✓; right side bhi (b◊c)□a = ba + 2ca ✓.
Answer: B, D

q: Consider two set-associative cache memory architectures: WBC, which uses the write back policy, and WTC, which uses the write through policy. Both of them use the LRU (Least Recently Used) block replacement policy. The cache memory is connected to the main memory. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
opts: A read miss in WBC never evicts a dirty block
A read miss in WTC never triggers a write back operation of a cache block to main memory
A write hit in WBC can modify the value of the dirty bit of a cache block
A write miss in WTC always writes the victim cache block to main memory before loading the missed block to the cache
exp:
(A) False: WBC me read miss pe LRU victim dirty ho sakta hai, use evict (write back) karna padega.
(B) True: write-through me memory hamesha updated hai, koi block dirty nahi hota ⇒ write back ki zarurat nahi.
(C) True: write hit pe clean block ka dirty bit 0 → 1 ho jaata hai.
(D) False: WTC me victim ko memory me likhne ki zarurat nahi (already updated); aur write miss pe aksar no-write-allocate bhi hota hai.
Answer: B, C

q: Consider a 512 GB hard disk with 32 storage surfaces. There are 4096 sectors per track and each sector holds 1024 bytes of data. The number of cylinders in the hard disk is _________
exp:
Capacity = cylinders × surfaces × sectors/track × bytes/sector.
512 GB = 2³⁹ bytes.
Ek cylinder = 32 × 4096 × 1024 = 2⁵ × 2¹² × 2¹⁰ = 2²⁷ bytes.
Cylinders = 2³⁹ / 2²⁷ = 2¹² = 4096.
(Cylinders = tracks per surface.)
Answer: 4096

q:
The baseline execution time of a program on a 2 GHz single core machine is 100 nanoseconds (ns). The code corresponding to 90% of the execution time can be fully parallelized. The overhead for using an additional core is 10 ns when running on a multicore system. Assume that all cores in the multicore system run their share of the parallelized code for an equal amount of time.
The number of cores that minimize the execution time of the program is ________
exp:
Serial part = 10 ns, parallel part = 90 ns.
n cores: T(n) = 10 + 90/n + 10(n − 1).
T(1) = 100, T(2) = 10 + 45 + 10 = 65, T(3) = 10 + 30 + 20 = 60, T(4) = 10 + 22.5 + 30 = 62.5.
Calculus: 90/n² = 10 ⇒ n = 3.
Minimum at n = 3 cores.
Trap: 2 GHz clock distractor hai, use nahi hota.
Answer: 3

q: A given program has 25% load/store instructions. Suppose the ideal CPI (cycles per instruction) without any memory stalls is 2. The program exhibits 2% miss rate on instruction cache and 8% miss rate on data cache. The miss penalty is 100 cycles. The speedup (rounded off to two decimal places) achieved with a perfect cache (i.e., with NO data or instruction cache misses) is _________
exp:
Har instruction ka I-cache access: stall = 0.02 × 100 = 2 cycles.
Sirf 25% instructions data access karte hain: stall = 0.25 × 0.08 × 100 = 2 cycles.
Actual CPI = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
Perfect cache CPI = 2.
Speedup = 6/2 = 3.00.
Trap: data miss ko 0.25 se multiply karna mat bhoolo.
Answer: 3.00

q:
Consider the following code snippet using the fork() and wait() system calls. Assume that the code compiles and runs correctly, and that the system calls run successfully without any errors.
(see code)
The total number of times the printf statement is executed is _______
exp:
Har iteration me har existing process fork karta hai ⇒ processes double, aur har process ek baar printf karta hai.
Iteration 1: 2 processes ⇒ 2 prints.
Iteration 2: 4 processes ⇒ 4 prints.
Iteration 3: 8 processes ⇒ 8 prints.
Total = 2 + 4 + 8 = 14. (wait() sirf order badalta hai, count nahi.)
Answer: 14

q:
Consider the entries shown below in the forwarding table of an IP router. Each entry consists of an IP prefix and the corresponding next hop router for packets whose destination IP address matches the prefix. The notation "/N" in a prefix indicates a subnet mask with the most significant N bits set to 1.
Prefix | Next hop router
10.1.1.0/24 | R1
10.1.1.128/25 | R2
10.1.1.64/26 | R3
10.1.1.192/26 | R4
This router forwards 20 packets each to 5 hosts. The IP addresses of the hosts are 10.1.1.16, 10.1.1.72, 10.1.1.132, 10.1.1.191, and 10.1.1.205 . The number of packets forwarded via the next hop router R2 is _______

Let G = (V, Σ, S, P) be a context-free grammar in Chomsky Normal Form with Σ = {a, b, c} and V containing 10 variable symbols including the start symbol S. The string w = a³⁰b³⁰c³⁰ is derivable from S. The number of steps (application of rules) in the derivation S →* w is _________
exp:
CNF me length n ki string derive karne ke liye exactly 2n − 1 steps lagte hain.
(n − 1 rules A → BC, aur n rules A → a.)
|w| = 30 + 30 + 30 = 90.
Steps = 2 × 90 − 1 = 179.
Trap: 10 variables wali info irrelevant hai.
Answer: 179

q: The number of edges present in the forest generated by the DFS traversal of an undirected graph G with 100 vertices is 40. The number of connected components in G is _________
exp:
DFS forest me har connected component ka ek spanning tree hota hai.
k trees aur n vertices wale forest me edges = n − k.
40 = 100 − k ⇒ k = 60.
Answer: 60

q:
Consider the following two regular expressions over the alphabet {0,1}:
r = 0* + 1*
s = 01* + 10*
The total number of strings of length less than or equal to 5, which are neither in r nor in s, is _________
exp:
Length 0..5 ke total strings = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 16 + 32 = 63.
r: ε aur 0ᵏ, 1ᵏ (k = 1..5) ⇒ 1 + 10 = 11.
s: 01ᵏ (k = 0..4) ⇒ 5, 10ᵏ (k = 0..4) ⇒ 5 ⇒ 10.
Common (r ∩ s): '0' aur '1' ⇒ 2.
|r ∪ s| = 11 + 10 − 2 = 19.
Neither = 63 − 19 = 44.
Trap: ε ko bhoolna ya '0','1' ko double count karna.
Answer: 44

q: Consider a memory management system that uses a page size of 2 KB. Assume that both the physical and virtual addresses start from 0. Assume that the pages 0, 1, 2, and 3 are stored in the page frames 1, 3, 2, and 0, respectively. The physical address (in decimal format) corresponding to the virtual address 2500 (in decimal format) is _________

A bag contains 10 red balls and 15 blue balls. Two balls are drawn randomly without replacement. Given that the first ball drawn is red, the probability (rounded off to 3 decimal places) that both balls drawn are red is _________
exp:
Pehla ball red diya hua hai ⇒ ab bag me 9 red, 15 blue (total 24).
Both red | first red = P(second red | first red) = 9/24.
= 0.375.
(Formula se bhi: (10/25 × 9/24)/(10/25) = 9/24.)
Answer: 0.375

q:
Consider a digital logic circuit consisting of three 2-to-1 multiplexers M1, M2, and M3 as shown below. X1 and X2 are inputs of M1. X3 and X4 are inputs of M2. A, B, and C are select lines of M1, M2, and M3, respectively.
Circuit: M1 has input-0 = X1, input-1 = X2, select S1 = A, output Q1. M2 has input-0 = X3, input-1 = X4, select S2 = B, output Q2. M3 has input-0 = Q1, input-1 = Q2, select S3 = C, output Y.
For an instance of inputs X1=1, X2=1, X3=0, and X4=0, the number of combinations of A, B, C that give the output Y=1 is _________
exp:
X1 = X2 = 1 ⇒ Q1 = 1 (A kuch bhi ho).
X3 = X4 = 0 ⇒ Q2 = 0 (B kuch bhi ho).
Y = Q1 jab C = 0, Y = Q2 jab C = 1 ⇒ Y = 1 sirf jab C = 0.
C = 0 fix, A aur B free ⇒ 2 × 2 = 4 combinations.
Answer: 4

q: Consider sending an IP datagram of size 1420 bytes (including 20 bytes of IP header) from a sender to a receiver over a path of two links with a router between them. The first link (sender to router) has an MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) size of 542 bytes, while the second link (router to receiver) has an MTU size of 360 bytes. The number of fragments that would be delivered at the receiver is ________
exp:
Data = 1420 − 20 = 1400 bytes.
Link 1: max data = 542 − 20 = 522 ⇒ multiple of 8 ⇒ 520. Fragments: 520, 520, 360.
Link 2: max data = 360 − 20 = 340 ⇒ multiple of 8 ⇒ 336.
520 → 336 + 184 (2 fragments), 520 → 336 + 184 (2), 360 → 336 + 24 (2).
Reassembly sirf receiver pe hoti hai, router already-fragmented packets ko aur fragment karta hai.
Total = 6.
Trap: 1400/336 ⇒ 5 lena galat — fragmentation link-by-link hoti hai.
Answer: 6
